title: Microsoft may have finally fixed Windows search by turning it into a chatbot
key_facts: At the company's San Francisco Surface event on Wednesday (7 Oct 2026), Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's executive vice president of Windows and Devices, demoed a new Windows Search experience.
From this fall, the Search menu accepts short typed commands for thousands of actions, such as dark mode, do-not-disturb, a mic-volume slider, or sending a text from a paired phone.
Users can converse with the Copilot app from the search menu without launching it; Microsoft says the search is faster and more efficient.
Microsoft also announced Hybrid Intelligence: local AI models on the PC, with cloud inference still used for the hardest tasks.
Engadget notes the change comes less than a year after Microsoft promised to remove unnecessary Copilot integration from Windows 11.
Copilot features powered by Hybrid Intelligence roll out to Windows PCs over the coming months.
quote_evidence: Less than a year after it promised to remove unnecessary Copilot integration from Windows 11, Microsoft announced today that it plans to turn part of the operating system's Task Bar into a sort of chatbot.
Starting this fall, the Search Menu will allow you to carry out thousands of different actions across Windows just by typing short commands into its interface.
why_it_matters_hint: Everyday Windows users get AI actions from search; the features were shown, not yet shipped.
